activities.anchor: Every living thing is built on carbon chains
activities.caption: rank the four accounts by balance
activities.name: cccReservoirOrder

config.prompt: Four great reservoirs — put them in order, largest balance first:
items: Oceans — about 38,000 GtC, the giant account
config.why: The smallest account is the one that matters most this century: a few hundred billion tonnes moved quickly is the whole story of the climate.

activities.anchor: the natural greenhouse effect is the reason Earth is habitable
activities.caption: true or false — the blanket itself
activities.name: cccBlanketJudge

statements.s: CO₂ is simply pollution with no useful role.
statements.why: The argument is strictly about the extra blanket being added, not about the blanket itself.

statements.s: With no heat-trapping gases at all, Earth's average surface would be near −18 °C instead of +15 °C.
statements.why: The natural effect is worth 33 °C — it is why the planet is habitable.

statements.s: The dispute is about the added thickness of the blanket, not its existence.
statements.why: Ten thousand years of balance at ~280 ppm is the baseline the extra line item bends.

statements.s: Ozone flips its verdict with altitude, like CO₂ flips with amount.
statements.why: Good up high, bad nearby — the same summary shape as the blanket argument.

activities.anchor: No other dataset in environmental science is as famous
activities.caption: put today's CO₂ on the ppm scale
activities.name: cccKeelingPlace

config.prompt: Where does today's atmospheric CO₂ sit on this scale (ppm)?
config.why: Past 420 ppm — the highest in at least 800,000 years of ice-core record, up from 280 before the industrial era.

activities.anchor: at a price: dissolved CO₂ forms carbonic acid
activities.caption: pair each ledger with its character
activities.name: cccLedgerMatch

config.prompt: Four accounts, four tempi — pair ledger with character:

pairs.right: the fast one — a heartbeat of months
the slow one — dead roots hold about three times the carbon of all living plants
the colossus — quietly absorbed roughly a quarter of all human emissions
the original thermostat — about 0.1–0.2 GtC/yr, with hands too slow for a century-scale jolt

config.why: The ocean's favour has a price: surface pH has slipped from about 8.2 to 8.1 — a 30 per cent jump in acidity that stresses shell-building life.

config.prompt: At 10 GtC per year emitted and a 45% airborne fraction, the air gains about 2.1 ppm each year. Roughly how many years to add 100 ppm at that pace?
config.why: Under half a century — and the panel is linear: halve the emissions (or the airborne fraction) and the years double.
config.context: Underneath the diplomacy of every climate negotiation, this is exactly what the two sides argue about.

activities.anchor: How can a trace gas matter at all?
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the mechanism in two moves
activities.name: cccIrcloze

config.text: The Sun's energy arrives mostly as visible light, which nitrogen, oxygen and CO₂ all ignore; it warms the surface, and the surface re-radiates that energy as %%0%% — which nitrogen and oxygen stay passive to, but CO₂, water vapour and methane absorb and re-emit in all directions, including back %%1%%. Eunice Foote (1856) and John Tyndall (1859) demonstrated the heat-trapping; %%2%% calculated in 1896 that doubling CO₂ would warm the planet by several degrees.
config.hint: Their molecules flex and vibrate at exactly those wavelengths — 0.042% of the air, doing all the work.

activities.anchor: Why are scientists confident the added CO₂ is
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the fingerprint argument
activities.name: cccFingerprintSpot

config.prompt: A student's fingerprint summary contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Fossil carbon is ancient, so it is depleted of carbon-13 and contains no carbon-14.
Atmospheric ratios of both isotopes shift exactly as burning old carbon predicts — the Suess effect.
Atmospheric oxygen is rising in lock-step with the CO₂ rise, since combustion releases it.
Ice cores show 800,000 years in which CO₂ never left the 180–300 ppm band — until the last two centuries.
config.correction: Atmospheric oxygen is DECLINING in lock-step — combustion consumes O₂ as it releases CO₂.
config.why: Isotopes, oxygen and ice cores — independent lines, one conclusion: the added CO₂ is ours.

config.prompt: Once warming starts, the system answers — file each response:

items.label: warmer air holds more water vapour — itself a heat-trapping gas
ice–albedo: white reflective surface replaced by dark absorptive ocean
how clouds will respond — the hardest to model

config.why: Feedbacks, not linearity, are why the response of clouds remains the largest single uncertainty in the whole field.
